summary: Crash and/or data corruption upon attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks
description: The bug Attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks causes the player to be unable to respawn. The game crashes (Exception generating new chunk caused by java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException), and/or the world is corrupted (java.nio.channels.OverlappingFileLockException: null), and you become unable to open it again. "Negative index in crash report handler (0/15)" is spammed to the debug log. To reproduce 1. Create a new world. 2. Execute /worldborder center 50000000 50000000. 3. Execute /kill. 4. You are unable to respawn. 5. Attempt to go to title screen. 6. The game crashes, or the world becomes unable to be opened again.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new world.
3. Execute the command `/worldborder center 50000000 50000000`.
4. Execute the command `/kill`.
5. Observe that you are unable to respawn.
6. Attempt to go to the title screen.
7. Observe that the game crashes, or the world becomes unable to be opened again.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 21w39a, 21w40a, 21w41a, 21w42a, 21w43a, 21w44a, 1.18 Pre-release 1 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior: The actual behavior of the bug occurs when a player attempts to save a world with a world border center set over 30 million blocks, leading to the inability to respawn. Upon executing the command to set the world border center to these coordinates, and subsequently using the /kill command, the game fails to allow the player to respawn, resulting in a crash. This crash is characterized by an exception related to new chunk generation, specifically an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, which indicates that the game is attempting to access an invalid index in the chunk data. Additionally, there is a risk of world corruption, as indicated by the occurrence of an OverlappingFileLockException, which prevents the world from being opened again. The debug log becomes cluttered with repetitive messages stating "Negative index in crash report handler (0/15)," further highlighting the issue. To reproduce this behavior, one must create a new world, set the world border center to 50 million blocks in both coordinates, execute the /kill command, and then attempt to respawn or navigate to the title screen, where the game will either crash or the world will become inaccessible.
Expected Behavior: When attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks, the player should be able to respawn without any issues. The game should successfully save the world and allow the player to return to the title screen without crashing or corrupting the world. The debug log should not display any error messages related to negative indices or file lock exceptions, ensuring a smooth gameplay experience.
